title: Oncall experience snapshot and safe-playbook transformer
author: Jordan Kim
description: Context: On large incidents we repeatedly see noisy, inconsistent handoffs and long warmup times for responders. This PR introduces two tightly-coupled utilities: (1) an ephemeral Oncall Experience Snapshot (OES) generator that collects a concise, scrubbed telemetry bundle + mini-visualization (treemap of impacted services, latency/error hotspots) and (2) a Safe-Playbook Transformer (SPT) that converts human-written runbooks into an executable checklist with embedded safety gates and a dry-run similarity score. Motivation: reduce time-to-first-action, standardize handoffs, and make runbooks both machine-consumable and safety-aware so auto-remediations remain conservative. This is a single, focused PR because the integration surface is small but cross-cutting: snapshot capture, sanitization, small UI export (handoff card), and a Transformer service library used at ingest and in the incident-bot Slack flow. Changes: implements snapshot format v0.2, sanitization heuristics, a treemap generator for telemetry rollup, the Transformer DSL (matchers -> step templates -> safety checks), a dry-run library to score transformed playbooks against historical incident traces, and a small Slack attachment formatter. Checklist: - [x] Snapshot capture + sanitizer implemented - [x] Transformer DSL + tests - [x] Dry-run scoring harness with mocked traces - [x] Slack handoff card output - [x] Unit/integration CI green - [x] Docs: developer guide and operator notes linked Related work: Linear ENG-1429 (oncall handoffs), SRE-77 (playbook safety). There are no infra-cost changes; feature flag `oes_spt.enabled` added for staged rollout. Notes: description intentionally compact; see commits and changed_files for details.

release_notes: Adds Oncall Experience Snapshot (v0.2) and Safe-Playbook Transformer: generates sanitized incident snapshots, treemap visualizations, and converts human runbooks into executable checklists with safety gates and a dry-run similarity score. Feature gated behind `oes_spt.enabled`.
rationale_summary: Shorter, cleaner handoffs reduce cognitive load and mean responders can quickly triage; transformer reduces manual errors in playbooks and enables safe partial automation. The design biases safety (conservative gates and dry-run scoring) over aggressive automation.
notes_on_safety: Transformer always annotates steps with `safety_level` and refuses to generate automated remediation tasks with safety_level >= critical. Dry-run score is advisory only; operator must opt in to enable auto-execution via `autoexec.playbooks.allow` flag. Snapshot data is sanitized using a strict PII policy; no raw tokens or credentials are stored in the handoff card.
